title: Gibbs variational principles and Boltzmann irreversible theorem
authors: Mário J. de Oliveira, Silvio R. Salinas
abstract: We analyze the Gibbs variational principles associated with the probability distributions of (i) an isolated system and (ii) a system at constant temperature. We give an example of using the Gibbs inequality to obtain the free energy and analyze the phase diagram of an Ising model with competing interactions. We also review the Boltzmann irreversible theorem, and show how it is connected to the Gibbs variational principles. This connection is established by using the Kolmogorov equation for the evolution of the probability distribution, which predicts a monotonic increase of entropy for an isolated system, and a decrease of the free energy for a system in contact with a thermal reservoir.
summary: This paper unifies concepts from equilibrium and non-equilibrium statistical mechanics by showing that the Gibbs variational principles are mathematically equivalent to the Boltzmann irreversible theorems. Using stochastic evolution equations, it derives bounds on entropy increase and free energy decrease for both isolated and open quantum/classical systems.
main_problem: The paper analyzes Gibbs variational principles for systems isolated or at constant temperature, aiming to connect these principles rigorously to the Boltzmann irreversible theorems.
main_result: It establishes that both the first (entropy increase) and second (free energy decrease) Boltzmann irreversible theorems are mathematically equivalent to the corresponding Gibbs variational inequalities ($S_m \ge S$ and $F_c \le F$).
method: The analysis uses stochastic evolution equations, specifically a modified Boltzmann-Kolmogorov equation, alongside thermodynamic derivations involving free energy minimization.
model_or_system: The primary model studied is the Axial-Next-Nearest-Neighbor Ising (ANNNI) model on a cubic lattice. The framework extends to general open systems interacting with thermal reservoirs.
key_observables: Entropy ($S$), Free Energy ($F = U - TS$), and the time evolution of these quantities ($\mathrm{d}S/\mathrm{d}t$ and $\mathrm{d}F/\mathrm{d}t$).
important_parameters: Interaction coupling constants ($J_1, J_2$) defining the ANNNI Hamiltonian; temperature $T$; and system volume/size.
main_assumptions: The derivation of irreversible theorems relies on assuming specific forms for transition rates (detailed balance) and utilizing inequalities like Jensen's inequality.
figures_summary: Not specified, but the analysis involves deriving equations of state and phase diagrams for the ANNNI model using variational methods.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first defining Gibbs principles for isolated/canonical systems, then introducing a generalized Boltzmann-Kolmogorov equation to describe time evolution. It subsequently derives the irreversible theorems ($\mathrm{d}S/\mathrm{d}t \ge 0$ and $\mathrm{d}F/\mathrm{d}t \le 0$) and finally proves their equivalence to the variational bounds.
why_interesting: This work provides a deep theoretical link between equilibrium statistical mechanics (variational principles) and non-equilibrium dynamics (irreversibility theorems), which is fundamental for understanding relaxation processes in complex quantum or classical systems.
